sections.h2: Who records deeds in Sanilac County
sections.html:
Any paper that changes or burdens title to land in this county is filed with the recorder in Sandusky. Deeds, mortgages, land contracts, easements, liens, plats, surveys and court orders about real estate all get indexed there, using one uniform system and fees fixed by state law.

Drafting is outside the office's job. Staff will not write a deed or give legal advice, so have an attorney or title agent prepare yours. Once a document exists, the office answers practical questions at (810) 648-2313, and the county's department page links to forms, fee schedules and requirements.

A weekly land transfer list is posted on the same site, naming the parties and the section and township for each deed that cleared that week. Browsing a few weeks of it shows what land is moving near yours. Bring the legal description from your current deed when you visit or call, so any question about your parcel can be answered quickly.

Plan on $30 to put a deed on record, plus $8.60 in transfer taxes per $1,000 of price. These are the charges a seller meets most often.

Sanilac County charges around a sale
ChargeAmount
Base fee to record a deed or mortgage (MCL 600.2567)$30, whatever the length
Added instruments in an assignment or discharge$3 each
Treasurer's tax certificate$5
County transfer tax (MCL 207.504)$1.10 per $1,000
State transfer tax (MCL 207.525)$7.50 per $1,000
Paper copies from the land records$1 a page, $5 to certify

Ask your closing agent to total these before the closing date so the figure on your settlement statement holds no surprises.

The seller does. State law puts the tax on the grantor and gives 15 days after delivery of the deed to pay the county treasurer, though at the Sanilac counter it is collected as the deed is recorded.

Put the full value of the land on the face of the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it. A sale that bundles a house with furniture or equipment is taxed on the real estate alone when the two values are written separately.

Some deeds owe no tax. The state exemptions include:

  • a transfer for under $100;
  • family transfers from a parent to a child and from a grandparent to a grandchild;
  • a court-ordered transfer with no price set by the order;
  • a land contract, until title actually passes.

The county act has no family exemption, so a gift deed can skip the state share and still owe the county share. A deed with neither a price nor an exemption cited is returned.

MCL 565.201 sets the intake checklist, and the county reposts it on its real estate information page. In short, signatures need dark ink with printed names beneath them, the grantee's address and the drafter's details belong on the page, and page one needs a 2.5 inch clear top margin and a first line naming the type of recordable event.

Social Security numbers must be cut back to their last four digits, and non-English text needs a translation attached. A deed that clears every point cannot be refused for its content, while one that misses a point is sent back and the closing waits.

Have the drafter read the checklist against the finished deed before anyone signs. Fixing a margin on a draft costs nothing, and fixing it after a notary has signed means starting over.

sections.h2: Do warranty deeds need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed does. The treasurer must certify the property's tax status first for $5. Land contracts, assignments of them and any deed containing a warranty covenant follow the same path.

The county's schedule lists no such step for a plain quit claim deed. A quit claim hands over whatever the grantor owns with no promise about title, which suits relatives and estate cleanups but leaves a paying buyer exposed, so market-price buyers usually ask for a warranty deed.

Median home value in the county is $168,300, so the transfer tax on a typical sale is a real number to subtract when you compare offers.

The office takes cash, checks, money orders and debit or credit cards, with checks payable to the Sanilac County Register of Deeds. Card payers at the counter show photo ID, and an online payment location exists for remote payers.

Searching costs nothing at rod.sanilaccounty.net, where guest users can look through an index that begins in 1801. Page images come as PDFs at $1 a page, with a $5 charge on every order.

The office also runs a free property fraud alert. Enroll a parcel and the owner is told whenever something new is recorded against it, which helps with a farm field or lake cabin that nobody checks for weeks.

The forms page carries three downloads: a warranty deed form, a quit claim deed form and an agricultural property affidavit form. The affidavit matters on farmland, where a buyer may need to state that qualified agricultural property will stay qualified agricultural property after the sale.

A separate packet covers manufactured homes. A seller whose home is a mobile or manufactured unit on owned land should ask the office about the Affidavit of Affixture, which the county lists beside the recording requirements and the transfer tax exemption statutes.

The same office is a U.S. passport acceptance facility, so a family selling a house and moving abroad can handle a passport application in the same trip. Hours and appointment rules change, so phone (810) 648-2313 before driving to Sandusky.

Sanilac County fronts Lake Huron in the Thumb, and at 963 square miles of land it is the largest Lower Peninsula county by that measure. The 2020 population was 40,611. There are 17,516 households and 21,972 housing units, a gap of roughly 4,450 homes that fits a county of lakeshore cottages and houses left empty after a death or a move to town. Owners live in 82.6 percent of homes, and monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,226 against a median rent of $807.

Local families and lake-home shoppers make up much of the buyer pool, and an inland farmhouse reaches a different audience than a cottage at the shore. Level, rich soil keeps farming at the center of many parcels, so a buyer may care more about acreage and drainage than about the house itself. The four cities are Sandusky, Croswell, Marlette and Brown City, and Lexington, Port Sanilac and Carsonville see seasonal visitors.

faqs.q: Where is the Sanilac County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in Sandusky, the county seat, and its phone number is (810) 648-2313. It records deeds and mortgages and does not prepare documents.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to record in Sanilac County?
faqs.a: The base charge is $30 for each document. A warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer's certificate, and transfer tax runs $8.60 per $1,000 of price, paid by the seller.

faqs.q: Can I search Sanilac County land records without an account?
faqs.a: Yes. The guest login at rod.sanilaccounty.net searches the index at no cost, and page images are $1 each plus a $5 order fee.

faqs.q: Which forms does the county offer for a farm or family sale?
faqs.a: The forms page lists a warranty deed, a quit claim deed and an agricultural property affidavit. Have an attorney check any form against your facts before you sign.

faqs.q: How far back do the online land records go?
faqs.a: The index at rod.sanilaccounty.net starts in 1801. Searching is free for guests, and image copies are $1 per page plus a $5 fee per order.
